newsitem.title: UK: South West Water up in strong water sector.
newsitem.headline: South West Water up in strong water sector.

text.p: Shares in UK water companies held their early gains by midday Wednesday following upbeat comment in the Financial Times on the sector's prospects and with analysts at brokerage UBS also positive.

UBS analyst Lakis Athanasiou said South West Water, up 17-1/2p at 656 by 1224 GMT, was his favourite stock in the sector, followed by Hyder Plc, up 15p at 792-1/2 and then by Thames Water Plc and Severn Trent Plc.
Thames was up 16p at 641 and Severn Trent was up 14p at 703-1/2.

Echoing comments in the FT's Lex column, Athanasiou said the sector looked attractive in the medium term regardless of "windfall" tax policies ushered in by the Labour party, well placed to win an election that must be held by the end of May.
He said there was 20 percent potential upside in the sector and that water stocks should perform well in the second half of the year, once the uncertainties of Labour's plans had been allayed.
Real dividend growth in the sector should on average be a robust eight percent through to the year 2000 despite Labour's plans, he said.
However the UBS analyst said he did not favour United Utilities Plc or Wessex Water Plc, arguing they were less attractive on dividend and valuation terms.
Earlier the FT's Lex column said UK utilities had been oversold on prospects for a Labour win and that water companies in particular had scope for further cost-cutting.
